name: archaeology
doc:
ARCHAEOLOGY - the decay clock read backwards (issue #11, 2026-10-16: reach, down the domain list). Every
radiometric age is one law, t = -(T_half / ln 2) ln(N/N0), SEALED here through archaeology.ARCH_VERIFY for the
radiocarbon clock (the Cambridge half-life 5730 yr and the Libby convention 5568 yr), for the long clocks
(potassium-40, uranium-238 at the age of the Earth), and for the half-life count n = -log2(f). The half-lives
are measured constants, CITED as postulates; the ages are theorems of the decay law and are SEALED. Calibration
against the atmospheric record is declined. Idempotent.

sticks.question: Archaeology - the decay clock, dated and sealed
sticks.statement: Every radiometric age is the exponential decay law read backwards: t = -(T_half / ln 2) ln(N/N0).
references: W. F. Libby, Radiocarbon Dating (1952; Nobel lecture 1960)
H. Godwin, Half-life of radiocarbon, Nature 195 (1962) 984
M. Stuiver & H. A. Polach, Discussion: reporting of 14C data, Radiocarbon 19 (1977) 355
A. H. Jaffey et al., Precision measurement of half-lives of U-235 and U-238, Phys. Rev. C 4 (1971) 1889

marks.claim: [one half-life, SEALED] Half the carbon-14 left means 5730 years: t = -(5730/ln 2) ln(0.5) = 5730 (sealed through archaeology.ARCH_VERIFY). The Cambridge half-life, 5730 +/- 40 yr (Godwin 1962), is the physical constant.
[two half-lives, SEALED] A quarter left is 11,460 years (sealed through archaeology.ARCH_VERIFY): each halving adds one half-life, so the clock is linear in the logarithm of what remains.

[the practical limit, SEALED] One percent left is 38,069 years (sealed through archaeology.ARCH_VERIFY): ln(0.01) = -4.605 half-lives of 1.4427 each. Below about one percent the count drowns in background, which is why radiocarbon reaches roughly 50,000 years and no further - the bound is the measurement, not the law.

[the Libby convention, SEALED] With the Libby half-life, 5568 yr, half remaining reads 5568 years (sealed through archaeology.ARCH_VERIFY, half_life_years = 5568). A conventional radiocarbon age is still reported on the 5568 scale (Stuiver & Polach 1977) and corrected later; the two scales differ by the factor 5730/5568 = 1.029. Two conventions, one law - and the convention is CITED, never confused with the constant.

[the potassium clock, SEALED] Potassium-40, half-life 1.248 billion years: half remaining is 1.248 Gyr (sealed through archaeology.ARCH_VERIFY, the same law with its own T_half). The potassium-argon clock dates the volcanic layers that bracket the fossils.

[the age of the Earth, SEALED] Uranium-238, half-life 4.468 Gyr: a sample with 49.44 percent of its original U-238 is 4.54 Gyr old (sealed through archaeology.ARCH_VERIFY) - the age of the Earth from the uranium-lead clock (Patterson 1956, meteorite leads). The slow clocks reach what the fast one cannot.
[counting half-lives, SEALED] An eighth remaining is exactly three half-lives: n = -log2(1/8) = 3 (sealed through archaeology.ARCH_VERIFY).

[ten half-lives, SEALED] One part in 1024 is ten half-lives (sealed through archaeology.ARCH_VERIFY): after ten half-lives a thousandth is left - the rule of thumb for when a radioactive source is 'gone'.

[the half-lives, CITED] 5730 +/- 40 yr (Godwin 1962), 5568 yr (Libby, the conventional scale), 1.248 Gyr for K-40 and 4.468 Gyr for U-238 (Jaffey et al. 1971) are MEASURED constants: cited as postulates, never sealed. What is sealed is the arithmetic the law does with them.
marks.source: Godwin, Nature 195 (1962) 984; Stuiver & Polach, Radiocarbon 19 (1977) 355; Jaffey et al., Phys. Rev. C 4 (1971) 1889

marks.claim: [the assumption the clock rests on] A radiocarbon age assumes the starting ratio N0 is known - that the atmosphere's carbon-14 was constant. It was not (solar activity, the carbon cycle, bomb carbon), so a raw age is CALIBRATED against tree rings and corals (IntCal). The engine seals the decay arithmetic and declines the calibration: a calibrated date is inferred from a curve, never kept as the law's own output.
marks.source: P. J. Reimer et al., IntCal20, Radiocarbon 62 (2020) 725; the decay law assumes closed system + known N0

marks.claim: [on the one map] The decay clock is nuclear physics (card_floor_nuclear_physics: the exponential law and its half-life) read as a logarithm (card_floor_logarithm: t is proportional to ln of the fraction), applied to the Earth's record (card_floor_earth_science: radiometric dating). One law, three floors; this stick is where the archaeologist's spade meets the physicist's constant.
marks.source: the one map; card_floor_nuclear_physics, card_floor_logarithm, card_floor_earth_science
